## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/02.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Data, Data Everywhere
• NUMEROUS SGP analyses are conducted for MCAS analyses each
year (especially post-COVID)
1. There are two types of analyses based upon the growth norm
used: Cohort and Baseline referenced.
2. There are two types of analyses based upon backward and
forward looking analyses: SGP (norm-referenced) and SGP
Projections (criterion-referenced/growth-to-standard).
• 1 and 2 yield a total of four types of analyses, each with a number
of variables associated with them that are delineated below.</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/03.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">SGP
• SGP analyses are norm-referenced analyses that examine previous
student growth (backward looking) in a norm referenced fashion.
• Growth norms for SGP analyses can be derived from current (cohort-
referenced) or derived from prior data (baseline-referenced)
• SGP (cohort-referenced) and SGP_BASELINE (baseline-
referenced)
• Because SGP can be calculated using more than a single prior,
there are also (if requested) SGPs based upon the number of
priors used: SGP_ORDER_1, SGP_ORDER_2, … and
SGP_BASELINE_ORDER_1, SGP_BASELINE_ORDER_2, …</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/04.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">SGP Projections
• SGP analyses are criterion-referenced analyses that are forward looking and
utilize existing growth norms (either cohort or baseline-referenced) to
establish growth-to-standard trajectories across a designated time-frame.
• The most often used standard to reach is “proficiency”, but other
standards (e.g., “advanced”) are also utilized.
• The usual time frame is 3 years but other time frames can be established.
Massachusetts is considering 5 years.
• We can only project out to the extent to which there is available test data.
• We cannot monitor a student’s progress toward an outcome if there is
not assessment data available for the years/grades designated.</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/05.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">SGP Projections
• Trajectories (across a given time span: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, … years) can be established in two
ways:
• SGP metric:
• SGP_TARGET_X_YEAR cohort referenced
• SGP_TARGET_X_YEAR_BASELINE baseline referenced
• Scale score metric (SGP targets are converted back to scaled scores)
• SCALE_SCORE_SGP_TARGET_X_YEAR_PROJ_YEAR_Y
• SGPs are constant across the time span of the trajectory, but scale scores
are not. Therefore, for each year of the trajectory (YEAR_Y) we have a
different scale score.
• SCALE_SCORE_SGP_TARGET_BASELINE_X_PROJ_YEAR_Y</div>
```
